newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha static in slow pre-weekend trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha static in slow pre-weekend trade.

text.p: Naphtha prices were little moved in subdued Tokyo trade on Friday, traders said.
"The market is very Fridayish, very slow," one naphtha dealer said.

Open-spec naphtha offers were heard at $212.50 to $213.00 per tonne for first-half October against no firm bids. Bidding levels for the delivery period were notionally indicated at $211.00 to $211.50.
"The naphtha levels are purely notional. Once buyers start coming into the market with firm bids, sellers will become much more aggressive," another naphtha trader said.
The contango in naphtha's inter-month spreads became steeper, with second-half September/second-half October discussed at minus $1.50/minus $1.00, mirroring weakness in prompt cargoes, traders said.
Petrochemical firms in Japan have yet to cut their production despite declining prices for olefines and polyolefines in the region, naphtha dealers with petrochemical manufacturers said.
They added, however, that sluggish demand for ethylene, polyethylene and polypropylene is expected to eventually slow down petrochemical firms' spot naphtha purchases.
